scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Internal traffic between Office A and Office B works fine.
DSWs/CSWs report all OSPF neighbors Full. But Internet-bound
traffic (e.g., reaching 203.0.113.1) from any internal PC
times out. R1 itself can reach internal devices but cannot
reach the ISP gateways. Diagnose.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r1 default route
Mechanism: r1 is the only egress to the ISPs. Without a
  default route, packets destined to public IPs (anything
  not in 10.0.0.0/8 or 203.0.113.0/30) have no next hop on
  r1 and are dropped. Internal traffic stays inside the
  OSPF domain so it's unaffected. The fact that r1's
  OSPF neighbors are still Full distinguishes this from
  an OSPF daemon failure.
Localization: r1
Root cause: default route missing from r1's routing table
Fix: re-add default — `ip route add default via 203.0.113.1`
  (or restart frr if it was sourced via OSPF default-information
  originate from an ISP)
scenario.fix_spec:
re-add default — `ip route add default via 203.0.113.1`
  (or restart frr if it was sourced via OSPF default-information
  originate from an ISP)

agent.diagnosis_text: R1 is missing a static default route pointing to its ISP upstream gateways (ISPA at 203.0.113.1 and/or ISPB at 203.0.113.5). R1's FRR configuration includes `default-information originate` under `router ospf`, but this directive only redistributes a default route into OSPF if R1 itself already has a 0.0.0.0/0 entry in its routing table. Because no such entry exists, R1 never generates the OSPF external Type-5 LSA that would propagate a default gateway to CSW1, CSW2, DSWs, and the downstream access switches and PCs. Internally the topology is fully converged — all OSPF neighbor adjacencies are Full and all intra-domain 10.x.x.x prefixes are exchanged correctly — so Office-A to Office-B traffic is unaffected. Internet-bound packets from any PC arrive at their first-hop DSW or CSW, where there is no default route, and are silently dropped. R1 itself can reach 203.0.113.1 and 203.0.113.5 directly (both are on connected /30 subnets via eth2 and eth3), but anything beyond those links (e.g. 172.253.62.100, 216.239.35.0) is unreachable because R1 has no forwarding path for non-locally-addressed traffic. The NAT MASQUERADE rules on R1's eth2/eth3 are already correct. The corrective fix is to add static default routes on R1: in FRR, enter `ip route 0.0.0.0/0 203.0.113.1` and `ip route 0.0.0.0/0 203.0.113.5` (for dual-ISP redundancy). Once R1 holds a default route, `default-information originate` will generate the OSPF external LSA, propagate 0.0.0.0/0 to all OSPF-speaking devices, and internet traffic will flow through R1's NAT.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names R1 as the affected device and discusses its missing default route and OSPF behavior.
The agent explicitly identifies the missing default route (0.0.0.0/0) on R1 and describes adding static defaults to restore connectivity.
The report explicitly states OSPF adjacencies are Full and intra-domain prefixes are exchanged, distinguishing the missing default from an OSPF daemon/adjacency failure.
Proposes adding the missing default route(s) on R1 (0.0.0.0/0 via 203.0.113.1 and optionally 203.0.113.5), which matches the expected remediation.

The log shows R1 has only connected 203.0.113.0/30 routes and no 0.0.0.0/0 entry, can ping the ISP gateways, and the agent observed downstream devices lack an OSPF-injected default; the conclusion that R1's missing default route prevents internet egress follows logically and the proposed fix matches. Minor truncations obscure a few exact config lines, but the core observations and inferences are present and consistent.
